info.name: ClinicalHarmony · Phase 5b slice 1 — HL7 validator vs US Core 6.1.0 + Silver builds
info.description: The official HL7 FHIR validator against US Core 6.1.0 (POST /api/fhir/validate, public) and Silver → US Core FHIR → Gold builds (POST /api/fhir/build[/patients/{id}], needs clinicalharmony/pipeline.write). Needs docs/db-init/16 and 17 applied. Make sure `docker-compose up -d` is running. Run '0b. Auth' first: it does a client_credentials grant against Keycloak (realm clinicalharmony, {{keycloak_url}}) and stores the token in the collection variable access_token, which every request inherits via the collection's Bearer auth (public endpoints ignore it). Tokens live 5 minutes — re-run 0b when you get 401s.

request.description: Expect: 200 OK, body `{"status":"UP"}`. If this fails, the container isn't running — check `docker ps` for clinicalharmony-fhir-compliance-service.

SMART Backend Services-style client_credentials grant (client secret via HTTP Basic). Requests every SMART read scope plus the clinicalharmony/pipeline.write operational scope; the test script stores the token in {{access_token}}, which the collection's Bearer auth sends on every request. Expect: 200 with access_token, token_type Bearer, expires_in 300, and scope echoing what was granted.

Expect: 200 with compliant=false. No meta.profile, so it's checked against us-core-patient automatically. Violations (errors first) include Patient.gender and Patient.identifier (missing — each with a suggestedFix), and Patient.name[0].family (empty string). Send an X-Correlation-Id header to see it echoed back and stamped on the service's log lines.
Expect: 200, compliant=true, errorCount=0. One WARNING (dom-6: no narrative) is a best-practice note, not a failure.

Expect: 200, compliant=true, profile=us-core-observation-lab (picked because category=laboratory). LOINC code existence is a WARNING (no terminology server here — ontology-service owns that check). Change the UCUM code to 'percent' to see a real ERROR.

item.name: 13. HL7 validate — not a FHIR resource

request.description: Expect: 400 {"error":"Invalid FHIR resource", ...}. Only unparseable / non-FHIR payloads get 400; a non-compliant resource is still a 200.

Expect: 200, one result per silver.patients row. Seed patients SEED-0001 and SEED-0002 are fully compliant; SEED-0003 (deliberately bad) has a non-compliant Patient (Patient.name) and Condition (Condition.code). Then in DBeaver: SELECT resource_type, fhir_id, is_us_core_compliant, compliance_notes FROM gold.fhir_resources WHERE fhir_id LIKE 'silver-%'. Re-running is idempotent (upserts, same 18 rows).
Expect: 200 for an existing silver.patients id (3 = the deliberately bad seed patient); 404 for an id that doesn't exist.
